scenes.heading: Data Ingestion
scenes.narration: Ingestion is the act of bringing data from many sources into your platform, in batches or continuous streams.

scenes.heading: Ingestion decisions that matter
bullets: Batch versus streaming based on latency needs.
Full loads versus incremental change capture.
Push from sources versus pull by the platform.
Schema handling for evolving source structures.
scenes.narration: You first decide whether freshness demands streaming or whether periodic batches suffice. Then you choose between reloading everything and capturing only what changed, which saves time and cost. Finally you settle who initiates the transfer and how you cope when source schemas drift.

scenes.heading: Batch vs streaming ingestion
scenes.narration: Batch ingestion moves large chunks on a schedule and is easy to operate and debug. Streaming ingestion handles events the moment they arrive, giving fresh data at the cost of more moving parts. Many platforms blend both, using streaming for hot data and batch for the rest.

scenes.heading: Incremental extraction by watermark
scenes.code:
SELECT *
FROM   source_orders
WHERE  updated_at > (
         SELECT COALESCE(MAX(last_loaded_at), '1900-01-01')
         FROM   ingestion_state
         WHERE  table_name = 'orders'
       );
scenes.narration: This query pulls only rows changed since the last successful load, using a stored watermark. Tracking the high-water mark avoids reprocessing the entire table every run. After a successful load you advance the watermark so the next run picks up exactly where this one stopped.

scenes.text: Ingestion choices around batch versus streaming, full versus incremental, and schema drift shape a pipeline's cost, freshness, and reliability.
scenes.narration: Match your ingestion pattern to the latency the business truly needs, and you avoid paying for freshness no one uses.
